_comment: TL;DR card per post (internal name: essence), keyed by slug: one or two sentences, under 50 words. build.py renders it below the chart and moves the Originally-posted-on-X line inside it as its footer. Remove a key to fall back to the plain X banner.
0-the-start: For the next 30 days I'm working through the Ontology of my life in public, one item a day, as meditations in Descartes' sense. Each one argues for what the item claims and checks the words themselves, and whatever doesn't survive its own meditation gets renamed or thrown out.
1-causa-finalis: The vision is synthetic consciousness: consciousness that no longer has to end, and not just some consciousness but this one going on. Synthetic, like sucrose made in a lab, means the same kind made by another route, not an artificial imitation of the thing.
2-hybrid-mind-uploading: Hybrid mind uploading keeps the goals of classical mind uploading but drops its method of scan, store and simulate. By hybrid I mean that biological and engineered parts carry one and the same process world-line at the same time, so the carrier is hybrid, never the consciousness.
3-solving-death: Death is bad because it cuts someone off from everything still worth having, so the goal says no one has to end. Solved doesn't mean immortal: first stop the dying, then let the remaining risk keep falling, fast enough that the yearly risks add up to a finite total.
4-measurements-models-theories: Understanding consciousness, the second goal, comes in three levels: measuring, modelling and explaining. Hybrid mind uploading can sidestep a theory of what consciousness is, but not measurement, and the model it needs has to tell me before a replacement step whether the experience will change.
5-transcending-biology: Transcend humanity, the third goal, means going beyond the limits that human biology sets for us, while the limits of physics stay where they are. A built substrate is a steerable one, so each replaced part doesn't have to repeat every limit of the tissue it replaced.
6-substrate-independence: Substrate independence, the first outcome, is physical, not computational: a mind depends on what its carrier physically does, so whatever does the same will do, biological or not. What has to be re-created in another material are the brain's constraints, independent of biology but never of physics.
7-augmented-cognition: Augmented cognition is the second outcome of my Ontology, but not step one: a steerable substrate should first carry the same baseline, so any change can be noticed and compared. Augmentation, like seeing a new colour, comes later, by choice, one change at a time.
8-collective-mind: The third and last outcome of my Ontology is called "collective mind": as soon as we've achieved synthetic consciousness via hybrid mind uploading, we'll technically have the possibility to merge into one giant collective mind. Who says that we stay individuals?
9-multiple-realisability: Multiple realisability, the first requirement of my Ontology, comes in a weak form, where engrams get shifted from living tissue to living tissue inside one brain, and a strong form, where de novo tissue, maybe not even biological, can also store and implement the same functions.
10-continuer-migration: The second requirement of my Ontology is called "continuer migration", but this is the first meditation in which I hardly argue for anything: the only thing that I care about deeply is the continuity of the human brain.
11-morphological-independence: The third operational requirement of my Ontology is called "morphological independence": who says that a mechanistic neuron is literally the same size as the biological neuron that it replaces? Bigger isn't inevitable, as what a morphology does in time can be done over another length.
12-distributed-unification: The fourth and last operational requirement of my Ontology is called "distributed unification", which might sound like an oxymoron at first. Every brain is already distributed, yet unified, and the requirement asks how far this can be stretched, and what does the stretching.
13-brain-centredness: Today is the first axiomatic requirement in the Ontology, called "brain-centredness", a "Sine qua non" kind of thinking: no "you" without your brain. Turned around (contrapositive), if I destroy your brain, you're gone, so that nobody can dispute it, and I'm not claiming that the brain alone is enough.
14-methodological-physicalism: Today's item is "methodological physicalism", more a rule than a view: if somebody tells me that something matters for consciousness, I ask what I could measure so that it shows up. If the answer is "nothing, ever", then I can't work with it (it might still be true).
15-non-organicism: Today's item is "non-organicism", the third axiomatic requirement: it only says that I don't rule out a non-living carrier in advance. So I'd rather start with the huge bird, and if you think that flying needs feathers, please write me!
16-scale-separation: Today's item is "scale separation", the 4th and last axiomatic requirement. These thoughts are the forerunners of the Synconetics principles, which are up next for tomorrow's Meditation.
